Yes. 

Despite the brevity of the piece, both main characters—Jonas and Miriam—are developed as complex characters with distinct emotions, shared history, and internal conflicts. Through subtext and physical actions (like Miriam initially refusing to take off her coat, then finally draping it over the chair), we see them evolve and soften toward one another over the course of the conversation. Meanwhile, the waitress is appropriately kept as a flat, minor character; her brief, unobtrusive presence is natural to the café setting and serves merely to highlight the lingering synchronicity between the two protagonists (ordering the exact same drink at the exact same time) without feeling like a forced plot device.
